correctness.rationale: For ℓ=(1,3), ℓB−ℓ=(1/2,5/2) is nonnegative on the quadrant, so T≥n is precisely ℓB^(n−1)z<2 within the square. At n=3 the row is (11/4,39/4), giving both intercepts below one, and the coefficients thereafter increase. The exact area follows. The Perron vectors (1,ρ) and (1,2ρ) give ρ^(−j)ℓB^j→k(1,2ρ), yielding prefactor ρ/k². For T=n the two bounding inequalities become 2/k≤(1,2ρ)·w<2ρ/k in w=ρ^n z; these bounded regions converge in area and the rescaled density tends uniformly there to its positive value at zero. The linear slice length is proportional to the slice parameter, giving the stated entrance density on [c₀,c₁]. In the upper branch H=x+y−4/3 contracts by −1/2 and s=x+2y−2 changes sign. If |s|≤1/3 and the current point is in U, 3x+7y≤8 forces the next point to be in U; conversely an infinite upper itinerary has both phase limits in the square, forcing |s|≤1/3. Thus capture is exactly as described and amplitude is |s|. Both cutoff comparisons c₀<c₋ and c₊<c₁ reduce to 3ρ>1 using 2ρ²=3ρ+1. The cuts have zero limiting mass, so capture conditioning and the ratio of squared endpoints are justified. The phase density passes the normalization test and folds to constant 3. These are conditional limits for the stated density class, not finite-n uniformity or the law of eventual capture after recrossing. The frozen polygon checker was inspected, not executed; the proof is independent of its finite tests.

value.rationale: This quantifies which phases are actually selected by a well-defined rare event in a previously studied dynamical system. The exact capture fraction and cancellation of the signed bias after forgetting phase are information that the qualitative period-two attractor cannot supply. Conditioning on direct capture makes the law interpretable without conflating first entry with later returns.
